newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa critical but conscious in clinic.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa critical but conscious in clinic.

text.p: Mother Teresa was in critical condition but conscious on Sunday following surgery to clear two coronary artery blockages, an Indian heart clinic official said.
Doctors said long-standing lung and renal problems were a major concern, which could complicate the 86-year-old Roman Catholic missionary's heart condition and recovery.
"She is still critical," A.K. Chatterjee, administrator of Calcutta's B.M. Birla Heart Research Centre, told reporters when the clinic issued its regular evening bulletin.
"Mother is conscious and she spoke to medical staff," he added on Sunday, two days after surgery to clear the arteries.
Chatterjee said renal and lung problems had forced doctors to postpone treatment to correct her irregular heart rhythm.
The evening bulletin said: "Mother Teresa's condition is unchanged since the morning report. Physicians continue to monitor all her parameters very closely."
A midday bulletin said she remained in critical condition and her heart rhythm was still irregular. An earlier one said she was stable, comfortable and cheerful.
"Her long-standing lung and renal diseases continue to be a major concern, which could complicate heart condition and recovery," the midday bulletin added.
Chatterjee said Mother Teresa, who had chicken soup and fruit for lunch, had suffered from renal problems for the past two months and was receiving medication for them.
He described the lung problem as chronic. "At the age of 86 any problem is serious," he added.
Dr Tarun Praharaj, a member of her medical team, said: "She has got a chronic lung problem and borderline renal impairment."
On Saturday, American doctor Patricia Aubanel, another member of the team, said Mother Teresa had developed signs of bronchial pneumonia, which was being treated.
Mother Teresa, the 1979 Nobel Peace Prize winner and known as the "Saint of the Gutters" for her devotion to the poor, destitute and dying, was fitted with a heart pacemaker in 1989.
Dr D.P. Shetty, the medical team leader, told reporters early on Sunday that doctors were trying to correct with drugs her arrhythmia, or irregular heart rhythm.
"We are trying to correct her arrhythmia with medicine and we will watch her for two or three days.
"If it does not work, then only we have to go for mild electric shock or the mechanical cardioversion," he added.
Aubanel, who treated Mother Teresa in California in 1991, said cardioversion treatment for an arrhythmia was essential.
"It is absolutely necessary now for her to go for the cardioversion...There is some risk but she can't leave the hospital without this treatment," she added on Saturday.
"Our first choice is pharmacological cardioversion because Mother Teresa had refused to have electric shocks on a couple of occasions before," Aubanel said.
Mother Teresa, born of Albanian parents as Gonxhe Bojaxhi, was moved to the Birla clinic last Tuesday after entering the nearby Woodlands Nursing Home on November 22.
Nuns at the Calcutta headquarters of her Missionaries of Charity order prayed for her recovery on Sunday in a meeting that also included Hindus, Moslems, Sikhs and Buddhists.
"She is the only one who has done something for those with leprosy. We know that God will listen to our prayers and she will be alright," Sheikh Mukhtar, a leprosy patient, said.
The charity, with 456 centres in 111 countries, was founded by Mother Teresa in 1948.
